title: Turkish Airlines flight 634
summary: The Avro RJ100 crashed on final approach to Diyarbakır in thick fog conditions. The crew descended to 500 feet and below, well below the MDA of 2800 feet, despite poor visibility. The GPWS issued multiple alarms but the crew did not abort. The aircraft struck the ground 900 meters short of the runway threshold with a positive pitch angle.
probable_cause: The captain continued the descent below the MDA in thick fog conditions without visual references, continued to 500 feet and beyond with the GPWS alarming, and did not abort the approach in time.

factors.evidence: At the crash site and during approach, thick fog reduced visibility to as low as 1 meter at times
The captain violated standard procedures and continued the approach well below the minimum descent altitude of 2800 ft, descending to 500 ft and beyond
The ground proximity warning system started to trigger aural alarms at 1 mi off the threshold at 200 ft altitude
The crew did not initiate go-around procedure immediately upon GPWS alarm but delayed before deciding to abort, then crashed 8 seconds later
The airplane struck the ground with the undersurface of the fuselage and the landing gear 900 m short of the runway threshold

events.text: Flight 634 cleared to approach runway 34 from the south; weather report stated 3500 m visibility but thick fog was actually present
Aircraft at 5000 ft altitude when ATC instructed to continue approach and report when visual contact with runway established
Landing gear and flaps deployed as aircraft reached minimum descent altitude of 2800 ft but pilots had no visual reference to runway
Captain continued descent well below MDA to 500 ft and beyond looking for runway lights; at 1 mi from threshold and 200 ft altitude, GPWS alarmed
Crew decided to abort landing and initiated go-around but aircraft struck ground before maneuver executed

title: TANS Perú 222
summary: The Fokker F28 descended to Chachapoyas Airport in very poor visibility with no DME distance measuring capability. The crew was overconfident, failed to follow procedures, and did not use proper communication. The aircraft began its descent too early and crashed into a hillside 10 miles north of the airport at 3450 meters altitude.
probable_cause: Controlled flight into terrain due to crew overconfidence, lack of effective communication between crew, and premature descent initiation in conditions of very poor visibility without distance measuring equipment to confirm distance from airport.

factors.evidence: Very poor visibility conditions at Chachapoyas during approach
Flight began descent too early without DME distance confirmation, leading to impact 10 miles north of airport and 35 meters below Cerro Collorque summit
Poor communication and coordination between crew during descent
Landing checklist not followed, crew failed to follow published procedures
Aircraft crashed into vertical face of Cerro Collorque hill at 3450 m altitude, aircraft pulverized by impact

events.text: Departed Chiclayo at flight level 190 on heading 075 in very poor visibility
Aircraft turned left to heading 060, four minutes later began descent to flight level 130
Speed brakes deployed, slowing aircraft from 280 knots, initiated right turn to heading 135 to line up with runway 13
Aircraft descended too early without DME confirmation, crashed into vertical face of Cerro Collorque hill at 3450 m, 35 m below summit, 10 miles north of airport

notes: Death of co-pilot's father 4 days before not included as speculative factor

title: 2003 Iran Ilyushin Il-76 crash
operator: Aerospace Force of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps
summary: On 19 February 2003, an IRGC Aerospace Force Ilyushin Il-76 carrying 275 people crashed into the Sirch mountains southeast of Kerman, Iran, while flying from Zahedan to Kerman in poor weather with strong winds; there were no survivors. The aircraft lost contact with air traffic control at 5:30pm as villagers in the area reported hearing a loud explosion. Investigators concluded it was a controlled flight into terrain caused by deteriorating weather and high winds, though a militant group later claimed responsibility.
probable_cause: Investigators believe the crash was a controlled flight into terrain, citing deteriorating weather conditions and high winds.

factors.evidence: the four-engine ... aircraft lost contact with air traffic control at 5:30 pm after flying into poor weather conditions
Strong winds were reported in the region of the crash when the aircraft disappeared from radar
Investigators believe it was a controlled flight into terrain, citing the deteriorating weather conditions and high winds
A terrorist organization called the Abu-Bakr Brigades also claimed responsibility for the crash

events.text: The Il-76 was flying from Zahedan to Kerman in poor weather conditions with strong winds reported in the region.
The aircraft lost contact with air traffic control at 5:30 pm.
Villagers in the area described hearing a loud explosion around the time the aircraft disappeared from radar.
The aircraft crashed into the Sirch mountains, southeast of Kerman, killing all 275 aboard.
A terrorist organization called the Abu-Bakr Brigades claimed responsibility for the crash.

notes: text presents competing theories (weather CFIT vs midair collision speculation vs terrorist claim); investigators' stated conclusion (CFIT/weather) used as primary cause

title: UM Airlines 4230
summary: Charter flight transporting Spanish peacekeepers attempted to refuel at Trabzon Airport in dense fog with visibility below 10 meters. The pilot could not locate the runway on the third landing attempt and crashed into a mountain near Maçka 15 miles from the airport.
probable_cause: Dense fog with visibility below 10 meters prevented the crew from locating the runway, leading to controlled flight into terrain on the third landing attempt.

factors.evidence: it slammed into a mountain near Maçka
because of dense fog, visibility was less than 10 m
the pilot had stated that he could not see the runway
on the third attempt the aircraft tried to land in dense fog
on its third attempt to land in dense fog, the aircraft crashed into a mountain

events.text: The aircraft attempted to land at Trabzon Airport in dense fog with visibility less than 10 m.
The pilot stated that he could not see the runway on the first landing attempt.
Because of dense fog, the second landing attempt failed.
After two failed landing attempts, the aircraft made a third attempt to land in the fog.
The aircraft crashed into the side of a mountain near Maçka, 15 mi from Trabzon.

notes: visibility quantified as less than 10 m
pilot decision to continue after two failed attempts clear

title: UTAGE 141
operator: Union des Transports Aériens de Guinée
summary: A Boeing 727 departing Cotonou struck a building and crashed into the Bight of Benin during takeoff roll. The aircraft was significantly overloaded and boarding procedures were chaotic with no seat allocation. Combined with the short runway and high passenger demand, the aircraft could not achieve safe takeoff performance.
probable_cause: Aircraft overloading combined with short runway length and inadequate weight and balance procedures prevented the aircraft from achieving safe takeoff performance.

factors.evidence: Aircraft was overloaded; passengers boarded disorderly with no seat allocation and names not written on boarding passes.
Investigation revealed massive incompetence within the airline and dangerous safety culture.
Airline lacked adequate safety procedures and regulatory oversight.
Airline incompetence went unnoticed due to lapses in management oversight.
Aircraft struck a building during takeoff roll and crashed into the Bight of Benin.

events.text: Aircraft loaded in disorderly fashion with no seat allocation; boarding passes did not list passenger names allowing last-minute seat reselling.
Total of 86 passengers boarded at Conakry, 9 disembarked in Cotonou, 10 from Togo joined, aircraft at full capacity and overloaded.
Aircraft attempted takeoff from short runway at Cotonou on Christmas Day with overloaded passenger and cargo.
Aircraft struck building during takeoff roll and crashed into Bight of Benin.

notes: aircraft had been operated by multiple carriers
short runway at Cotonou was design constraint
